title: Task-side computational modeling and calibration data foundation
objective: Create deterministic, auditable task-side datasets for two pilot multi-step reasoning families without making claims about model-internal computation.
in_scope: Symbolic function-composition generator, solver, and renderer
Relational path-composition generator, solver, and renderer
Task-side dependency graphs and generator traces
Small fixtures, documentation, and automated tests
out_of_scope: Final commitment to paper task families
scientific_constraints: Task-side traces must not be represented as model reasoning traces
Candidate operation labels must remain provisional and family-local by default
Cross-family operation correspondences must be optional hypothesis metadata
Structural nuisance factors must be independently configurable where feasible
Negative or infeasible balance checks must fail visibly rather than be hidden

interfaces.name: TaskFamily
responsibilities: solve or verify from the canonical problem
emit dependency graph and task-side trace

files.purpose: unit, property-style, integration, determinism, and CLI tests

outputs.name: canonical_splits
outputs.retention: small fixture committed; larger data external

acceptance_checks: Same configuration and seed produce byte-identical records and equal content hashes
Every target is recomputed and verified from its canonical problem
Dependency graphs are acyclic and trace-consistent
Semantic instance identities do not overlap across exclusive splits
Requested factor cells are satisfied or generation fails loudly
Both families and all split types appear in the smoke fixture
Full local test suite passes on Python 3.11
CLI smoke run requires neither model weights nor network access
Manifest contains resolved configuration, seed, versions, counts, distributions, and hashes
No large artifact or machine-specific absolute path is committed

steps: Generate the larger configuration twice into scratch storage
Compare hashes and validate all records
Record runtime, peak RAM, storage, environment, and Git revision
